q: Which transformation most clearly represents internal RNA editing?
A. Removal of a 5′ leader from tRNA|B. Conversion of an internal A to I in pre-mRNA|C. Addition of a poly(A) tail|D. Excision of an ordinary spliceosomal intron
A-to-I changes a retained nucleotide. Leader removal, polyadenylation and intron excision define termini or splice boundaries; they are maturation but not this class of editing.
The direct chemical product of adenosine deamination is:
Deamination converts adenine to hypoxanthine while preserving the ribose linkage. Inosine may be decoded as G but is not guanosine; pseudouridine derives from uridine.
Which RNA feature is generally required for classical ADAR recognition?
A. A double-stranded region|B. A poly(A) tail alone|C. A free amino acid|D. A 5′ triphosphate alone
ADARs recognize duplex RNA. The duplex may be intramolecular. The other features do not supply the characteristic structural substrate.
At the GluA2 Q/R site, CAG becomes CIG. Which amino acid is specified after editing?
CIG is interpreted like CGG, an arginine codon. CAG specifies glutamine, not glutamate. The first and third bases remain C and G.
The apoB-48 product arises primarily because:
A. A long intron is retained|B. ApoB-100 is cleaved at residue 48|C. CAA is converted to UAA|D. ADAR changes a U to C
APOBEC1-associated C-to-U editing introduces an in-frame stop. This shortens translation, not necessarily RNA length. Neither proteolysis at residue 48 nor ADAR is the primary mechanism.
Which substrate is directly consumed during uridine insertion editing?
Uridylyl transferase incorporates UMP from UTP into RNA. dUTP is a deoxynucleotide; SAM donates methyl groups, and UDP-glucose does not supply this RNA residue.
Which component supplies sequence information in classical kinetoplastid uridine insertion/deletion editing?
A. Ribosomal 5S RNA|B. Spliceosomal U1 alone|C. DNA ligase|D. Guide RNA
Guide-target pairing positions insertions or deletions. Ribosomal RNA and U1 have different roles; the joining reaction uses an RNA ligase, which does not itself provide the guide sequence.
In many plant plastid editing systems, which proteins are important for site recognition?
A. Histones|B. PPR proteins|C. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases|D. DNA helicases
PPR motifs can recognize RNA sequences and position editing machinery. The alternatives are not the characteristic determinants of plant organelle C-to-U editing.
Which mammalian cytoplasmic rRNA is generally transcribed separately by Pol III?
5S is a separate Pol III product. 18S, 5.8S and 28S are derived from the large Pol I precursor.
An ITS sequence in mammalian pre-rRNA is:
A. A mature ribosomal protein|B. A tRNA anticodon|C. A DNA promoter not transcribed|D. An internal transcribed spacer removed during maturation
ITS separates mature rRNA regions in the precursor and is transcribed before removal. It is neither a protein nor an untranscribed promoter.
Why is the eukaryotic 80S ribosome not called 100S?
A. The S values describe sedimentation and are non-additive|B. It loses 20 nucleotides|C. 60S is actually 40S|D. The large subunit is not an RNA-containing particle
Sedimentation reflects mass and frictional properties, which change upon association. S does not count residues and the large subunit contains several rRNAs.
The characteristic methyl donor for fibrillarin is:
SAM transfers a methyl group and becomes S-adenosylhomocysteine. ATP and UTP supply nucleotides or energy in other reactions; NADH is a redox cofactor.
Which modification is guided by canonical box H/ACA snoRNPs?
A. DNA methylation|B. CCA addition|C. RNA pseudouridylation|D. Pol II CTD phosphorylation
H/ACA guides position a uridine for isomerization by dyskerin/Cbf5. CCA addition, DNA methylation and protein phosphorylation use separate enzymes.
Pseudouridine differs from uridine mainly in:
A. A C–C linkage between base and sugar|B. Absence of ribose|C. Addition of three nucleotides|D. Replacement by guanine
Ψ is an isomer with a bond between ribose C1′ and uracil C5. The RNA retains its sugar and nucleotide count. It does not acquire guanine.
Which statement about U3 snoRNA is most accurate?
A. It is a tRNA-charging enzyme|B. It is the 3′ CCA sequence|C. It is a bacterial DNA promoter|D. Its main established role includes early pre-rRNA processing
U3 is a box C/D snoRNA with an important role in early small-subunit maturation; not every member of that family is an ordinary methylation guide.
In a typical bacterial rRNA operon, which enzyme makes important early cuts in duplex precursor regions?
A. APOBEC1|B. RNase III|C. DNA polymerase I|D. Fibrillarin
RNase III cleaves duplex RNA. Subsequent enzymes refine rRNA ends; neither a deaminase nor a DNA polymerase performs this initial RNA cleavage.
Which enzyme removes the 5′ leader of many pre-tRNAs?
A. RNase Z|B. RNase P|C. CCA-adding enzyme|D. ADAR2
RNase P establishes the 5′ mature boundary. RNase Z commonly participates at the 3′ end, CCA-adding enzyme extends it, and ADAR2 edits duplex RNA.
Which statement correctly qualifies the catalytic composition of RNase P?
A. All forms are protein only|B. All forms are RNA only in vivo|C. RNase P is a DNA polymerase|D. Many are RNA-protein enzymes, but protein-only forms exist
The bacterial catalytic RNA discovery does not imply every RNase P is identical. Human mitochondrial RNase P is a protein-only exception.
A CCA-adding enzyme typically extends the tRNA by:
A. Adding CTP-derived C, CTP-derived C and ATP-derived A at the 3′ end|B. Reading a DNA template|C. Adding AAA to its 5′ end|D. Joining the anticodon to mRNA
The specialized nucleotidyltransferase performs template-independent 3′ extension. The correct sequence is CCA, not AAA; anticodon interaction is unrelated.
Which bond is typically cleaved in tRNA leader removal?
A. Peptide bond|B. Disulfide bond|C. RNA phosphodiester bond|D. Hydrogen bond only
RNase P catalyzes backbone hydrolysis, producing defined RNA termini. Noncovalent recognition contacts assist the reaction but are not the bond cleaved.
Which modification explains the T in the familiar TΨC loop?
A. Deoxythymidine|B. A deleted uracil|C. Ribothymidine|D. Guanosine
Ribothymidine is methylated uridine with ribose. It does not imply that tRNA contains DNA in that loop.
Which assay is most directly suited to testing whether an rRNA precursor retains ITS1?
A. A probe specific to ITS1|B. An antibody to DNA polymerase|C. Measuring total cellular ATP|D. Counting chromosomes
An ITS1 probe detects transcripts containing the spacer. The other measurements do not establish whether this specific RNA segment is retained.
Which event can change an internal RNA base without changing residue count?
A. Intron excision|B. CCA addition to an incomplete end|C. Uridine insertion|D. A-to-I editing
A-to-I changes the base chemically while preserving the backbone and length. The other choices remove or add residues.
Assertion: ADAR2 deficiency can impair a protein product even when the coding DNA is unchanged. Reason: ADAR2 can alter the base read by a ribosome.
A. Both true; reason explains assertion|B. Both true; reason does not explain assertion|C. Assertion true; reason false|D. Assertion false; reason true
The RNA-level chemical event can change a codon and therefore a protein without a genomic mutation. The reason supplies the causal mechanism.
Assertion: 5S rRNA is not part of the typical mammalian 47S precursor. Reason: 5S rRNA is generally transcribed by Pol III separately.
A. Both true; reason explains assertion|B. Both true; reason does not explain assertion|C. Assertion true; reason false|D. Assertion false; reason true
Separate polymerase III transcription explains the absence of 5S from the large polymerase I precursor.
Assertion: A box C/D guide can determine a specific rRNA methylation site. Reason: The guide itself must catalyze methyl transfer without protein.
A. Both true; reason explains assertion|B. Both true; reason does not explain assertion|C. Assertion true; reason false|D. Assertion false; reason true
Guide complementarity and offset position specify the target, but fibrillarin catalyzes the transfer in the canonical snoRNP.
Assertion: Every tRNA gene must contain a DNA-encoded CCA sequence. Reason: Mature tRNAs generally require CCA at their acceptor end.
A. Both true; reason explains assertion|B. Both true; reason does not explain assertion|C. Assertion true; reason false|D. Assertion false; reason true
CCA is important for mature function but can be added without a template. The requirement for a product does not mean its complete sequence must be DNA-encoded.
Assertion: A U-to-Ψ modification can escape detection by ordinary sequence-letter comparison. Reason: Uridine and pseudouridine are isomers rather than different standard sequence letters.
A. Both true; reason explains assertion|B. Both true; reason does not explain assertion|C. Assertion true; reason false|D. Assertion false; reason true
Conventional cDNA sequencing does not directly reveal the change of glycosidic linkage. Modification-sensitive assays are necessary.

Choose the correct statements: I. A-to-I preserves RNA length. II. APOB C-to-U can create a stop codon. III. All plant mitochondria use kinetoplastid guide-mediated insertion. IV. tRNA introns always use spliceosomes.
A. I and III|B. II and IV|C. I and II|D. III and IV
I and II describe correct mechanisms. III incorrectly generalizes a lineage-specific pathway, and IV confuses typical tRNA splicing with pre-mRNA splicing.
Match (1) fibrillarin, (2) dyskerin, (3) RNase P, (4) CCA-adding enzyme to (a) 5′ leader removal, (b) ribose methylation, (c) pseudouridylation, (d) terminal extension.
Fibrillarin transfers methyl groups, dyskerin isomerizes U, RNase P removes the leader, and the nucleotidyltransferase restores CCA.

Which statements about bacterial and eukaryotic rRNA maturation are valid? I. Both use precursors. II. In E. coli, 5S may be co-transcribed with 16S and 23S. III. Mammalian 5S is normally cut from 47S. IV. Eukaryotic rRNA modification often uses snoRNPs.
A. II and III only|B. I and III only|C. All four|D. I, II and IV
I, II and IV are correct. III is false because mammalian 5S is separately synthesized by Pol III.
Match (1) APOBEC1, (2) ADAR2, (3) uridylyl transferase, (4) RNA ligase with (a) fragment joining, (b) C-to-U, (c) A-to-I, (d) U insertion.
The two deaminases act on different bases, while transferase adds U and ligase seals RNA fragments.

Which statements are correct? I. The sequence of a mature rRNA is not measured in S units. II. A spacer probe can identify precursor RNA. III. A 3′ trailer is always retained on mature tRNA. IV. A mature tRNA may carry modified bases.
A. I and III|B. I, II and IV|C. II and III|D. III and IV
S is sedimentation, spacer probes identify retained precursors, and tRNA bases are often modified. A trailer ordinarily must be removed.
Matched DNA is A. A cDNA assay finds 144 G and 96 A observations at a candidate A-to-I site. What is the estimated editing fraction?
Use edited/(edited+unedited) = 144/240 = 0.60. 40% is the unedited fraction; 150% uses the edited-to-unedited ratio as a percentage. It is not a percentage of cells.
In the steady-state editing model k = 0.4 h⁻¹ and d = 0.1 h⁻¹. If d rises to 0.4 h⁻¹ without changing k, how does the edited fraction change?
A. 80% to 50%|B. 40% to 10%|C. 20% to 80%|D. It cannot change
Initially 0.4/(0.4+0.1)=0.8. Subsequently 0.4/(0.4+0.4)=0.5. The edited fraction depends on loss as well as editing; a decline need not imply reduced catalysis.
A hypothetical pre-rRNA is 9,200 nt. Retained products contain 1,800, 160 and 4,700 nt. What fraction of the precursor is removed, to the nearest percent?
The retained total is 6,660 nt; removed = 2,540 nt. 2,540/9,200 = 27.6%, approximately 28%. 72% is retained; other answers do not conserve the given lengths.

A C/D snoRNA D box begins at guide position 38. Positions 33, 34, 35, 36 and 37 pair with target positions 203, 202, 201, 200 and 199 respectively. Which target is methylated under the canonical rule?
The fifth upstream guide position is 38−5=33. It pairs with target 203. The pairing orientation prevents simply subtracting five from the target number.
Of 600 tRNAs, 250 lack all CCA, 150 end in C, 100 end in CC and 100 already end in CCA. How many CTP and ATP molecules are required for complete extension?
A. 650 CTP and 500 ATP|B. 1,200 CTP and 600 ATP|C. 500 CTP and 650 ATP|D. 750 CTP and 400 ATP
CTP = 2×250 + 150 = 650; ATP = 250+150+100 = 500. The complete 100 consume no substrate. The other options ignore partial termini or interchange substrates.
A tRNA precursor has 12 leader residues, 9 trailer residues and a 15-residue intron. Its total length is 110 nt, and CCA is not encoded. What is the mature length after complete processing?
Remove 12+9+15=36 nt, leaving 74; add three CCA residues to obtain 77. 74 omits addition; 80 adds six; 113 ignores removals.
In the precursor model, synthesis is 90 molecules/min and degradation is 0.1 min⁻¹. Processing falls from 0.8 to 0.2 min⁻¹. What are the new steady-state precursor number and processing flux?
P=90/(0.2+0.1)=300; flux=0.2×300=60/min. The original state was 100 molecules and 80/min; 450 neglects degradation; 90 confuses synthesis rate with precursor number.

A target mitochondrial transcript undergoes insertion of 11 U residues and deletion of 5 U residues within its coding region. Its unedited coding-region length is 294 nt. What is the net length, and can the length alone establish a functional reading frame?
A. 300 nt; yes|B. 300 nt; no|C. 310 nt; yes|D. 288 nt; no
Net change = +11−5=+6; length =300. Divisibility by three is necessary for a complete uninterrupted triplet count but cannot prove correct local sequence or absence of premature stop codons.
Matched DNA is G at a site where the reference genome is A, and all sense-oriented cDNA reads are G. Which conclusion is best?
A. Complete A-to-I editing proven|B. C-to-U editing is certain|C. The gene must have been spliced|D. A genomic difference can explain the RNA; editing is not established
The individual's DNA already encodes G. A reference-only discrepancy is not evidence of editing. Neither C-to-U chemistry nor splice junction changes are indicated.

An exon contains a candidate ADAR target. Disrupting an intronic complementary region reduces editing; a compensatory mutation restores pairing and editing without restoring the initial sequence. What is the strongest inference?
A. A duplex structure contributes to editing specificity|B. The original intron sequence is absolutely required|C. DNA replication is defective|D. All introns must be retained in mature mRNA

Restored pairing and editing after sequence changes support the structural requirement. The experiment does not prove all sequence effects are absent, nor does it require intron retention or altered DNA replication.
A knockout of an editing enzyme changes multiple RNAs. Genetically encoding arginine at the GluA2 Q/R site rescues survival without restoring the enzyme. What follows?
A. Every other edited RNA is restored|B. The enzyme never edits any other target|C. The Q/R product is a key determinant of the lethal phenotype|D. Genomic mutation and RNA editing are identical
This is a downstream bypass of a specific essential output, not restoration of all enzyme substrates. The rescued phenotype is survival, not a proof of universal molecular recovery.

A human intestinal reporter carrying CAA and its normal recognition element produces a short product. Changing that element suppresses C-to-U editing. A UAA version still yields a short product. What does the latter show?
A. APOBEC1 must cleave the protein|B. The recognition element directly causes peptide hydrolysis|C. Translation can terminate at UAA without the edit|D. UAA specifies glutamine
Genetically supplying the final stop bypasses the need for editing and tests downstream translation. The other answers confuse RNA conversion, proteolysis and the genetic code.
A kinetoplast editing reaction produces upstream fragments extended by the correct number of uridines, but no joined full-length product. Which step is the most direct candidate?
A. Ligase-mediated sealing|B. Initial UTP incorporation|C. DNA transcription termination|D. ADAR deamination
The presence of correctly extended fragments shows that cleavage and nucleotide addition occurred. Failure to seal fragments points to ligation or end compatibility, not initial U insertion.
A plant mutant retains C at one mitochondrial RNA site but other tested C-to-U sites are normal. Target DNA is unchanged. Which hypothesis is most specifically consistent with these data?
A. Complete loss of mitochondrial DNA|B. Global cessation of transcription|C. All RNA has become DNA|D. A site-specific recognition-factor defect

A restricted defect suggests a recognition component affecting that site, although further tests are required to establish identity. Normal other transcripts argue against global loss of DNA or transcription.
In a mammalian culture, newly synthesized 47S falls rapidly after a selective Pol I perturbation while new 5S remains initially unchanged. Why?
A. The two RNAs share the same promoter|B. 5S is normally produced by Pol III separately|C. 47S is a mature tRNA|D. 5S is produced by cleavage of protein
The immediate observation is consistent with separate transcription pathways. Later defects in assembly can influence 5S stability but do not contradict separate synthesis.
Deleting one C/D snoRNA reduces methylation at one target site. Fibrillarin abundance and methylation at unrelated sites are unchanged. Which interpretation is strongest?
A. Complete loss of all methyltransferase activity|B. Loss of a specific guide|C. All rRNA transcription is blocked|D. Pseudouridylation is necessarily absent throughout the cell
A local loss with preserved other sites fits a guide-specific defect. The data do not establish global loss of fibrillarin or pseudouridylation.
A proposed H/ACA target U is replaced by C, while compensatory guide changes restore pairing around it. No Ψ is detected at that position. Why?
A. Complementarity alone changes C into Ψ|B. Fibrillarin adds three U residues|C. The nucleotide is automatically deleted|D. Pseudouridine synthase requires a uridine substrate
Restoring guide positioning does not supply the chemically correct U substrate. Ψ is an isomer of U, not C. The alternatives describe unrelated or nonexistent reactions.
A tRNA maturation mutant accumulates molecules with intact 5′ leaders, correct 3′ ends and no introns. What is the most direct candidate step?
A. RNase P-dependent cleavage|B. CCA addition|C. Spliceosome-mediated mRNA cleavage|D. ADAR2 recoding
The retained leader specifically implicates 5′ processing, although a structural recognition defect can mimic RNase P loss. The 3′ end and intron status are already correct.
In two tRNA mutants, X accumulates intact intron-containing precursors; Y accumulates separate exon halves. Which assignment best explains this?
A. X: exon ligation; Y: splicing endonuclease|B. Both must lack RNA polymerase|C. X: splicing endonuclease; Y: exon ligation|D. Both must lack ADAR2
A cleavage block preserves the intact precursor; a joining block can leave separated halves. The inference assumes the observed intermediates are stable enough to detect.
A purified bacterial RNase P RNA cleaves precursor tRNA in a suitable ionic buffer, while the isolated protein does not. Which conclusion is warranted?
A. The protein is dispensable in every living cell|B. Every ribonuclease is a ribozyme|C. RNA can catalyze cleavage|D. Magnesium is the RNA template
The experiment establishes catalytic RNA activity under the tested conditions. It does not establish universal enzyme composition or physiological dispensability of associated protein.
A tRNA modification mutant shows normal initial transcription but a rapid decline of mature labeled tRNA during a chase. Which explanation is directly consistent?
A. Reduced tRNA stability|B. No transcription occurred|C. DNA replication has doubled|D. The tRNA necessarily gained a poly(A) tail
Normal initial labeling followed by rapid disappearance is consistent with increased degradation or destabilization, not loss of synthesis. The molecular degradation route needs further evidence.
Two tissues have equal total APOB RNA, but edited fractions of 10% and 90%. The protein output ratios differ less than the RNA ratios. What is the best explanation?
A. RNA editing is impossible|B. RNA fractions always equal protein fractions|C. All RNA is untranslated|D. Translation efficiency or protein stability can differ between products
RNA fractions are not automatically protein fractions. Product-specific translation, turnover and detection can change the observed protein ratio; the data alone do not select which factor.
A bacterial rRNA processing mutant accumulates a long RNA recognized by probes for both 16S and 23S plus a spacer probe. Mature RNAs are reduced. Which interpretation is most plausible?

A. The mature 16S and 23S must be covalently joined in every ribosome|B. Delayed separation or maturation of a polycistronic precursor|C. A mammalian Pol III defect|D. A new genomic deletion is proven
The long RNA contains both mature regions and spacer, consistent with a shared precursor that persists. It does not establish a DNA deletion or covalent linkage in mature particles.
A tRNA variant contains a complete CCA end but still fails a functional maturation assay. Which additional comparison is most useful?
A. Only genomic chromosome number|B. 5′ end, intron status, and modification/folding state|C. Only the length of 28S rRNA|D. Only the amount of poly(A) RNA
CCA is necessary but not sufficient. Other processing defects may block function despite a normal acceptor terminus. The unrelated measurements cannot resolve this tRNA-specific problem.
In a hypothetical RNA experiment, a mature-sized rRNA lacks a chemical modification but a second mutant retains an ITS and lacks mature rRNA. Which comparison best separates the defects?
A. Measure only gel length for both|B. Count DNA bases only|C. Measure only protein molecular mass|D. Modification mapping for the first, precursor/product analysis for the second
The first alteration may not change RNA length; a chemical modification assay is needed. The second alters precursor boundaries and is directly addressed using probes and size analysis.
A source of double-stranded RNA is deleted and a noncoding A-to-I event disappears, yet GluA2 editing remains unchanged. What follows?
A. Substrate structure can determine site-specific editing independently of other targets|B. All ADAR activity is absent|C. GluA2 is no longer translated|D. Every editing event changes a protein
Selective loss of one substrate-associated edit with preservation of another argues against global elimination of ADAR function. Noncoding edits need not recode protein.
One species has genomic T at a conserved coding position; a related species has genomic C but mature RNA U. Both produce the same amino acid. Which claim is justified?
A. The ancestral state is necessarily genomic C|B. Every species edits that position|C. Different DNA-to-RNA pathways can generate the same mature coding output|D. The two proteins must differ
The observed endpoint is shared despite a different maturation pathway. Ancestral reconstruction requires additional phylogenetic evidence; universal editing and protein difference do not follow.
traps: Editing is not mutation
Compare matched genomic DNA and RNA from the same sample; the original DNA can remain unchanged.
Inosine is not guanosine
G-like decoding and cDNA readout reflect interpretation, not chemical identity.
Editing need not change protein
Noncoding edits can alter RNA recognition or structure; even coding edits can be synonymous.
ApoB-48 is not a proteolytic fragment
CAA becomes UAA; translation terminates while downstream RNA can remain.
Organelle editing is not universal
Kinetoplast U insertion/deletion differs from plant C-to-U and neither applies to every organelle.
45S and 47S are not nucleotide lengths
S describes sedimentation; precursor nomenclature is organism/stage dependent.
5S is separate in mammals
Pol III supplies 5S; Pol I supplies 18S, 5.8S and 28S through a large precursor.
Not all C/D snoRNAs are conventional methylation guides
U3 participates in pre-rRNA processing.
The guide is not necessarily the catalyst
Fibrillarin and dyskerin perform the chemistry in canonical snoRNPs.
RNase P is not universally RNA-based
Many forms contain catalytic RNA; protein-only forms exist.
CCA is not always encoded
Non-templated addition and repair can supply the same terminal sequence.
tRNA splicing is not generally spliceosomal
Dedicated cleavage and ligation are the usual eukaryotic tRNA route.
A normal-sized RNA may still be immature
Chemical modifications or a single terminal nucleotide may be missing.
An increased precursor is not necessarily increased transcription
A processing bottleneck can elevate precursor while reducing product flux.
